title: Precision and adequacy are independent variables.
A button is not evidence of agency if the causal window has already closed.
Representational loss often returns as correction labor borne by bodies.
Geertz’s “shape of its career” makes provenance only half of the path.
A category becomes infrastructure when it is compiled through fields, thresholds, permissions, queues, and denials.
Circulation is a sequence of transformations, not neutral transport.
Burrow-Giles is useful because the Court moves from the camera class to a production path.
Geertz’s “natural history of signs and symbols” is a direct methodological warrant for replacing class labels with trajectories through use.
Representation can help make reality without exhausting the reality it helps make.
“Call the shot” converts skill from retrospective attribution into a prospective falsifiable claim.
The Copyright Office recorded 624 iterations but treated the number as irrelevant to whether Allen controlled the particular expressive result.
Correction is only real when the contested difference survives translation into a still-open intervention point.
Compilation can be obtained by freezing the source program inside its interpreter.
Self-application turns the specializer into a compiler and then into a compiler generator.
Markov did not build a model of Eugene Onegin’s poetry; he destroyed almost all of the poem to isolate dependence.
Eugene Onegin was evidence in Markov’s fight about independence, not the object his mathematics was designed to explain.
Geertz’s “artistic Markov process” is immediately subordinated to composition-in-performance.
The audience is not context around the Moroccan poem; it is an input channel into its production.
Geertz’s 1976 Markov metaphor and the HMM turn in speech recognition are a real chronological collision with no demonstrated genealogy between them.
Reflection shifts the cultural/computational boundary from “can the rules change?” to “what constrains legitimate rule-change?”
LLMs did not create the first machine system in which ordinary English commands changed a computational world.
The culture/computer boundary cannot rest on improvisation versus exact semantics because formally exact semantics can describe distributions of improvisatory outcomes.

The deeper cultural/computational difference may be that programs usually hold their operational ontology fixed during a run while social actors can renegotiate the categories defining the state space.
The surviving scientific boundary is not culture versus code but specified uptake versus underspecified uptake.
Even self-reference and recursion-theorem constructions do not require Turing completeness.
By 1980 researchers were not merely issuing English commands to computers; they were constructing named subroutines in English.
Natural-language ambiguity was made executable by closing a human–machine repair loop rather than by eliminating ambiguity.
When action must pass through representation, representation enters the causal machinery of the world.
Reduction is necessary for action, but omissions differ by recoverability.
The essay’s strongest invariant is not “human control” but a branch that was perceptible before it was selected.
The strongest revision of “call the shot” is “locate the commitment.”
Plural coordination requires common reductions without requiring a neutral common world.
An acceptable programming language explicitly places programs inside the domain of data.
Kleene’s recursion theorem permits an explicit interchange of program and data roles.
Turing’s universal machine makes the rules portable by putting them inside the machine as exchangeable description.
TruthfulQA generates false answers under greedy decoding at temperature zero.
TruthfulQA splits falsehood before decoding into failure-to-learn and successful imitation of false data.
Hallucination is not logically caused by stochastic decoding.
Metaobject protocols invalidate fixed language behavior as a necessary property of programming systems.
Maude makes the transition theory itself into data that another transition theory can execute.
Self-reference does not require a syntactic reflection primitive: Kleene’s theorem constructs it from specialization.
Cage deliberately relocates artistic responsibility from choosing outcomes to designing the questions that chance will answer.
Generative art is defined by ceding subsequent control, so loss of local steering can be a positive feature of the production path.
Wall Drawing 88 does not specify one final image; it specifies a family of admissible realizations.
Wall Drawing 274 stores not the decision but the authority to make the decision.
Wall Drawing 237 proves that even a highly specific instruction does not contain its own final geometry.
Wall Drawing 797 makes unpredictable execution drift the content of a deterministic instruction.
Wall Drawing 65 specifies randomness itself as an artistic operation.
LeWitt’s later account reopens execution after his 1967 essay had rhetorically closed it.
Wall Drawing 289 separates the persistent work from every temporary material realization.
LeWitt’s wall drawings split specification precision from realization variability into independent dimensions.
LeWitt moves the consequential branches almost entirely before execution.
Duchamp makes selection itself intentional while attempting to remove aesthetic preference from the selection criterion.
A prompt can itself be a copyrighted work even when the image it generates is not.
The more a prompt behaves like a program, the less copyright can monopolize the behavior it performs.
The Allen decision could not inspect the artistic object most necessary to evaluate prompt craft because Allen withheld the prompts.
“Re-rolling the dice” collapses two technically different iterative practices: blind resampling and closed-loop steering.
Prompt-to-Prompt proves that “prompt control” is not a property of the sentence alone but of the interface architecture that interprets it.
Attend-and-Excite separates an expressive decision written in the prompt from the mechanism that makes the machine obey it.
ControlNet makes “the prompt” only one channel in a vector of independently authored controls.
Textual Inversion allows an artist to create a new “word” whose meaning is a learned visual concept.
The Beijing Internet Court and U.S. Copyright Office draw nearly opposite inferences from prompt variation.
The same prompting act can be classified as insufficient authorship, personalized expression, or a statutory “arrangement necessary for creation,” depending on jurisdiction.
Alfred Bell makes “keep that” legally powerful only after the accident has arisen inside a human act of making.
Thaler closes the machine-as-author theory without deciding the prompt-user-as-author theory.
Samuelson, Sprigman, and Sag reject the requirement of a complete preexisting conception and explicitly defend exploratory iterative authorship.
The strongest U.S. opposition does not claim that detailed prompts are automatically authorship; it makes reflected conception the hinge.
Andrien creates an expressive-surplus problem for generative AI: an intermediary may contribute non-rote expression while still being legally incapable of authorship.
Andrien makes the difficult boundary not tool versus author but rote realization versus intellectual modification by the intermediary.
The prompt dispute contains two hidden thresholds: how much control exists and how much copyright requires.
There is no judicial “dissent” from the Copyright Office prompt rule; the opposition is distributed across commenters, foreign courts, and competing attribution theories.
Prompt expansion turns underspecification into a machine-controlled exploration variable rather than a defect to be eliminated.
Prompt expansion is not a compiler in the ordinary semantics-preserving sense because it deliberately invents values for unspecified variables.
Prompt optimization creates an invisible normative layer because “better translation” is defined by an objective function.
Automatic prompt optimization can make the machine teach the human how the machine prefers to be addressed.
Approval can convert machine-added prompt content from hidden intervention into an explicit human commitment.
In systems that rewrite prompts internally, the user may not be the author of the operative prompt the model actually receives.
The human-authorship doctrine moved from an open 1966 question to a formal 1973 administrative rule before Congress enacted the 1976 Act.
CONTU’s influential computer-as-tool model depended on a technical premise that modern generative systems no longer straightforwardly satisfy.
Generative iteration breaks the old conception/execution sequence by feeding execution back into conception.
The Copyright Office’s current “traditional elements of authorship” test began as a provisional question in its 1965 annual report.
The Copyright Office makes authorship technologically contingent: the same human intention could cross the copyright boundary after an interface upgrade.
Li v. Liu did not hold that negative prompts independently constitute authorship; it treated them as one component of a total creative workflow.
A negative prompt does not simply subtract a forbidden object; its effect depends on when and how guidance enters the diffusion trajectory.
An exclusion can be causally decisive while leaving no positive expressive trace that copyright can point to.
The negative prompt is an authored refusal: it controls the work by specifying what must not survive.
“Original intention” can be a retrospective fiction because intentions themselves are outputs of making.
Iterative prompting creates an identification problem: observed preference is jointly produced by user intention and model feedback.
A prompt trajectory records not only the artist learning the image but the artist learning to speak the model’s preferences.
If prompt and image constitute one practice object, model version becomes part of the work’s conditions of intelligibility.
Prompt artists sometimes treat the prompt and image together as the artwork, making copyright’s prompt/output split descriptively incomplete.
A raw prompt history is provenance but becomes evidence of control only when revisions are paired with predictions about what should change.
The prompt history may be the most informative authored artifact even when neither individual outputs nor the final prompt reveal the artist’s intervention.
Midway’s player is denied authorship not because the player lacks causal control but because the machine prestructures the reachable expressive space.
Stern Electronics defeats the proposition that trajectory control by itself makes the controller an author.
Stern Electronics suggests a narrower replacement for distributional authorship: authorship of invariants across variable realizations.
Copyright already treats the generating program and its audiovisual outputs as separable works, blocking automatic inheritance in either direction.
Authorship of a generator does not automatically imply authorship of every output it can emit.
The deepest legal disagreement is whether authorship requires control over a token or control over a distribution.
Prompt vocabulary is only the shallowest layer of AI craft; mature practice increasingly operates across representations.
Prompt craft includes learning specialized vocabulary that is useful precisely because ordinary language and model-effective language are not identical.
Model accommodation can become recursively self-confirming if accommodated user prompts are later reused as training data.
Prompt expertise can improve by adapting to a model while simultaneously becoming less faithful to the user’s natural language and original intentions.
Prompt templates can function simultaneously as artistic style, executable method, and legally unprotectable procedure.
A platform can improve its outputs while decreasing the artist’s empowerment.
Platformization can destroy artistic agency without deleting the model’s nominal capabilities.
A model glitch can become craft knowledge, making technical improvement capable of destroying an artistic technique.
Prompting may be legally weakest exactly where it is artistically most interesting: as a practice of discovering a machine’s local language.
The deepest split across the seven parents is not human versus machine but where unresolved expressive variables are allowed to close.
The expressive variable may not exist before the act that discovers it.
Control can be measured as how many distinguishable futures an action channel can reliably produce, not how many buttons an interface displays.
Unseen control is weaker than craft because empowerment couples controllability to what the agent can perceive.
Agency in a co-creative system has two opposite directions: how much the artist can change the system and how much the system can change the artist.
A creative assistant need not infer what the artist wants; it can preserve the artist’s capacity to decide later.
A creative interface cannot preserve distinctions it lacks enough variety to express or counteract.
The children converge on a new distinction: expressive agency depends on where freedom is located, not merely how much freedom exists.
Current U.S. copyright analysis permits human authorship to enter after generation through creative selection, arrangement, or modification.
“Keep that” is not one operation; it contains at least four different causal structures.
Representations can manufacture the magnitude they later display.
Partial evaluation turns input data into program structure without changing the computed result.
A configuration file can become code merely because it changes more slowly than the rest of the input.
Partial evaluation introduces a second control problem: deciding which computation happens now and which becomes future code.
The simulation’s dominant transformation was conditionalization rather than falsification.
Availability was repeatedly weaker than intervention across otherwise unrelated domains.
The observer network functioned as a lateral nervous system while the public board remained causally inert.
Distributed discourse was achieved without distributed cognition.
An omniscient analyst can reconstruct collective intelligence that no participant ever possessed.
The network’s most productive claims changed function as they travelled.
Representations do not merely operate in time; they allocate actionable time.
Maude states explicitly that executability is relative: the same formal statement can be non-executable at one level and executable at another.
A transition relation can be fully specified while the choice of which transition to take remains a separate programmable object.
The strongest surviving invariant may be not specified uptake but counterfactual control: changing the representation must change the receiver’s behavioral policy.
The target is not complete representation but warranted passage.
The simulation’s substantive and methodological outputs converge on one question: under what conditions may a description act?
The choice-space of a creative act can be produced by an earlier act rather than given in advance.
The strongest challenge to the “re-roll” account is not that iteration is labor but that intermediate results can alter subsequent human commitments.
High causal influence over a realized path can remain navigation inside a possibility space structured by somebody else.
Variable realizations do not erase authorship when recurring expressive invariants remain attributable upstream.
Nominal interface choice is weaker than an action channel whose alternatives produce reliably distinguishable future states.
The strongest evidence of exploratory authorship may be neither predicting the first result nor liking it afterward, but making a discovered difference govern what happens next.
Some generations are epistemic actions rather than candidate artworks.
The expressive variable may be born during making rather than selected from a pre-given list.
Later stabilization of a surprise does not travel backward and make the maker the originator of the surprise.
The authored object after surprise may be an invariant across transformations rather than the surprised feature itself.
Exploration differs from shopping when an intermediate artifact changes the operations the maker can subsequently perform.
Prompt craft may chiefly produce a local causal model of the generator rather than a protectable expressive object.
A generative system can shape not only answers but which distinctions the maker learns to ask about.
Creative control is a perceptible action-to-future channel, not a count of available controls.
Control decomposes into discovery, commitment, constraint, steering, stabilization, invariant origin, and possibility-space origin.
Authorship after surprise begins when an unforeseen difference becomes a constraint on the future.
Schön’s 1992 “Designing as Reflective Conversation” exists in two journal publications and should not be silently normalized.
